fixed.problem: Blocking 2 (review): OP-4 had no restart case. Writing the composed case turned up a real bug: a pause at the project's budget that got no further was never counted as no progress. Its second card read no_progress false, so each raise in Settings woke the task again (the loop OP-4 is meant to stop). keepPausedWork (session/runner.ts) compared a pause only with earlier Run rows whose outcome is 'paused'. A hard stop at the project's budget or the month's cap leaves a 'budget_exceeded' row, so it was never compared.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/budget-pause.test.ts 'd1109-oversize-pause, run C: a pause at the project's budget that got no further asks, across a restart (OP-4)' > 'paused twice without getting further, then a restart and a raise in Settings: no session starts, one question asks; Continue with a note goes on from the note' (second card no_progress false). packages/runtime/test/oversize-pause.test.ts 'OP-4: a hard stop at the project's budget (its Run row budget_exceeded) that got no further than the one before is a pause that got no further'. Both fail with the old runner.ts.
fixed.how: keepPausedWork now treats both outcomes as the task's earlier pause (KEPT_WORK_OUTCOMES = ['paused', 'budget_exceeded'] from estimates/model.ts). The composed case covers the whole path: runOne pauses the task at the project's budget. Raising it to CHF 0.04 in Settings (budget.set) and calling scheduler.tick() wakes it, and it pauses again with the same work (no_progress true; the card reads 'paused again without getting further', '... so it waits for you.'). The runtime is restarted (composeRuntime). Ticks start nothing. Raising to CHF 5 plus ticks starts nothing either: the old card is withdrawn as asked_again and one question card is open with options ['Continue','Cancel task'] and a note box. A second restart follows. Continue with a note goes through POST /requests/:id/answer: change_card.start is recorded, the continuing brief has the note (quoted) and 'The last two runs of this task did not get further: try another way, ...', the task is done and its budget is unchanged. The simulated clock moves a minute between sessions, because two runs in the same simulated millisecond sort by random id. Sibling: a first pause that wrote cart.html, then a run that wrote it again with the same content, is also no progress. Docs: runtime.md, ADR 0115 point 6.
fixed.check_in_the_app:
Bench, done on fixup-d1109-oversize-pause:
1. In a new project, set the project budget to CHF 0.01 in Settings. Add one coder task, 'Write the members map in map.md' (bench env FORERUNNER_BENCH_LONG and FORERUNNER_BENCH_USAGE=members map:20000). Start a session with CHF 2.00. It pauses at the project's budget.
2. Raise the budget to CHF 0.03. A session starts by itself, as the card says, and pauses again having written nothing. The Inbox card reads '"Write the members map in map.md" paused again without getting further' / 'It stopped before it wrote anything. Its last run changed no file and left the same list, so it waits for you.', with 'Raise it there; this card then asks how to go on.'
3. Quit and restart. The card is the same.
4. Raise the budget to CHF 2.00 and wait 2.5 minutes. No session starts. One card asks '... continue with a note on what to do differently, or cancel it.', with a note box, Continue and Cancel task.
5. Type a note and press Continue. The session's brief has the note and 'try another way', and the task is done.
Live check 4: the same with the real model, at a project budget just below the task's first steps.

tests_changed_for_design.why: This restores exact assertions the fixer had loosened. Each states the one fixed outcome of L3-left-3's label and OP-7's clause, with an old-to-new comment. Nothing was weakened.

new_problems: The executor makes run ids with platform newId (random within a millisecond; session/executor.ts:1053), not the store's monotonicId. Under a SimulatedClock that does not move, two runs of one task sort at random by (created_at, id). task-context's workerRuns can then read the older run as 'the last run': the new OP-4 composed case failed 2 of 4 concurrent runs until the test moved the clock between sessions. In production the timestamps differ, so only tests are affected. Suggested: the executor takes the id from monotonicId, or tests move the clock.

On the bench, a pause at an outer limit is woken only when the spend is under 80% of the raised limit. That much room nearly always lets the next call run and write a part, so a pause that got no further at the project's budget shows up mainly when a run's first call writes nothing (here the stand-in's 'look at the folder' call). This is not a defect. It means live check 4 should set a project budget just below the task's first steps, and raise it only a little, to see the question card.

Seen while walking and not changed (wording): the drawer and Tasks row of a no-progress pause still use the limit's label (see not_done), and the replaced card's Answered line is new ('Its new card asks how to go on.'). The session lead may want both in the U-089 entry.
notes_for_other_areas: Runner (session/runner.ts keepPausedWork): the task's earlier pause, which madeProgress compares against, is now its newest earlier work run with outcome in KEPT_WORK_OUTCOMES (['paused', 'budget_exceeded']). Before it was only 'paused'. Hard stops at the project's budget or the month's cap now count, so no_progress can be true at an outer limit. d1109-starts-engine (C3), when it changes wakeBudgetWaits to prepare instead of start: a no_progress card at an outer limit is now really produced. Keep it out of any automatic start and keep askAfterNoProgress.

request-words.ts budgetOutcome (person-facing, old -> new): a card withdrawn as 'asked_again': 'Closed: it no longer needs you.' -> 'Its new card asks how to go on.'. The question card (change_card.question true), or any Continue with continued_usd_micro 0, after Continue: 'Gave "X" CHF 0.00 more: a session started.' -> 'Went on with "X": a session started.' (without a recorded start: 'Went on with "X": the next session continues it.'). Continue with money is unchanged.
loop/kept-work-check.ts: KeptWorkCheckDeps gains clock?: Pick<Clock, 'monotonic'> (SystemClock by default). compose passes the daemon's clock in its one keptWorkChecker hunk.

apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts POST /sessions now does what closeByStart does: for each continuable card (fakeContinuing) in the started project it sets status withdrawn and change_card.outcome 'went_on_at_start' with started_session_id and started_session_time (UTC HH:MM of startedAt), and moves the task to ready with the reason 'this session goes on with it from where it stopped'. C3 changes to the start path should keep this.
